# Clinical Case Summary — Implant In-Charge Review
**Case Type:** the patient & Pterygoid Implant Reconstruction | **Current Phase:** 2 — Surgical Placement | **Approval Status:** Pending Phase 1 Implant In-Charge Sign-Off

---

**A. the patient Information & Chief Complaint**

The the patient is a 65-year-old retired male presenting with severe maxillary atrophy as the primary complaint. The degree of atrophy, combined with the planned the patient and pterygoid anchorage strategy, indicates a substantially compromised residual maxillary ridge that precludes conventional implant-supported rehabilitation without zygomatic and pterygoid engagement. All mandibular teeth are charted as present (FDI 31–48), providing a full opposing natural dentition — a critical load-bearing consideration for the definitive prosthesis.

---

**B. Procedure Type & Treatment Rationale**

The planned intervention is a combined the patient and pterygoid implant reconstruction of the maxillary arch, targeting full-arch fixed rehabilitation without sinus grafting or extensive ridge augmentation. Pterygoid implants provide posterior anchorage in the pterygomaxillary complex where residual native bone remains, while zygomatic implants bypass the atrophic alveolus entirely by engaging the the patient as the primary osseous substrate. This extra-maxillary anchorage philosophy permits immediate loading with a screw-retained provisional prosthesis, which is the evidence-supported standard for this modality — deferred or removable loading is contraindicated in this architecture.

---

**C. Clinical Examination Findings**

Data pending for this phase. Formal documentation of ridge contour, keratinized mucosa width, soft-tissue biotype, and occlusocervical restorative height must be recorded and submitted by the treating clinician before Phase 1 gate approval can be granted. CBCT-derived ridge dimensions should correlate with intraoral findings at the time of surgical entry.

---

**D. Occlusal Analysis**

The the patient presents with a complete mandibular natural dentition (FDI 31–48), which creates a full-arch occlusal load against the planned maxillary fixed prosthesis — a scenario that demands rigorous occlusal scheme selection. A lingualized or mutually protected scheme with anterior guidance offloading posterior implant-supported segments is recommended. Parafunctional screening (bruxism, clenching history) must be documented; if positive, night-guard provision post-delivery and reinforced prosthetic framework design are mandatory. Vertical dimension of occlusion and available restorative space data are pending clinical submission.

---

**E. Aesthetic Risk Assessment**

At 65 years of age, a low-to-moderate smile line is statistically more probable, which may reduce anterior aesthetic risk; however, formal smile-line classification and lip mobility assessment must be recorded. Soft-tissue biotype documentation is outstanding — thin biotypes demand particular attention to transmucosal emergence profile and abutment selection in Phases 3 and 4. Given the atrophic maxilla, SAC classification for this case is **Complex**, necessitating experienced operator execution and implant in-charge oversight at each approval gate.

---

**F. Medical Assessment & ASA Classification**

Medical data have not yet been formally submitted for this case. Given the the patient's age (65) and the physiological demands of the patient and pterygoid surgery — which involves deeper anatomical dissection, longer operative times, and proximity to the orbital rim and pterygopalatine structures — thorough medical clearance is non-negotiable. ASA classification must be formally assigned; any ASA III or higher designation requires specialist medical liaison and may influence anaesthesia modality (local with sedation vs. general anaesthesia) and perioperative antibiotic and corticosteroid protocols.

---

**G. Implant Selection & Planning**

Implant system, dimensions, and per-site CBCT analysis are pending Phase 1 data submission. ZAGA (the patient Anatomy-Guided Approach) classification must be recorded per side: the ZAGA class (0–4) directly determines the surgical entry point and the degree of buccal cortical engagement versus intrasinusal trajectory. A ZAGA 0 or 1 (flat or gently concave anterior the patient) permits a more classic sinus slot approach, while ZAGA 3–4 (deeply concave or buccally prominent anatomy) mandates an extrasinus or exteriorized trajectory with the implant head positioned laterally to the sinus wall to avoid soft-tissue complications. Pterygoid implant angulation planning (typically 45–55° to the occlusal plane) must be confirmed against CBCT sagittal cross-sections to ensure engagement of the pyramidal process and pterygoid plates without encroachment on neurovascular structures.

---

**H. Surgical Approach**

Surgical data are pending submission and supervisor/implant in-charge approval. For reference, the expected approach involves a crestal and para-crestal full-thickness flap with buccal releasing incisions extending to the infraorbital region bilaterally for zygomatic access. The ZAGA-classified entry point per side will dictate whether a sinus window is created (intrasinus approach) or the implant traverses entirely external to the sinus membrane (extrasinus). Pterygoid site preparation requires a divergent posterior drilling trajectory with careful depth control confirmed radiographically.

---

**I. Implant Placement & Primary Stability**

Insertion torque values for the patient and pterygoid implants are the primary intraoperative stability metric; ISQ resonance frequency analysis is not applicable or clinically interpretable for these anchor types and should not be recorded. Insertion torque thresholds for immediate loading in this modality are typically targeted at ≥35 Ncm at the zygomatic and pterygoid sites, though bicortical purchase quality and tactile resistance throughout the osteotomy are equally weighted in the intraoperative stability assessment. These values must be documented per implant at the time of surgery.

---

**J. Bone Augmentation**

In the classical the patient and pterygoid reconstruction philosophy, horizontal and vertical alveolar augmentation is intentionally avoided by redirecting anchorage to extra-alveolar bone. However, if buccal dehiscences are encountered at the zygomatic implant emergence site — particularly in ZAGA 3–4 anatomy — localized soft-tissue or particulate graft coverage may be indicated to protect the implant body at the crestal exit point. Augmentation decisions should be documented intraoperatively and submitted with Phase 2 surgical records.

---

**K. Prosthetic Components & Closure**

In adherence to the immediate-loading protocol mandatory for this reconstruction type, a screw-retained provisional fixed prosthesis must be delivered on the day of surgery (Day 0). Removable or tissue-supported temporization is not an acceptable interim solution in the zygomatic implant protocol, as it applies compressive load to the healing soft tissues overlying the implant emergence sites and disrupts early peri-implant stability. Clinical checkpoints must be scheduled at **Day 0** (prosthesis delivery and occlusal verification), **Day 7** (wound inspection, screw-torque check, soft-tissue healing assessment), and **Day 30** (radiographic review, occlusal equilibration, early osseous response evaluation). The Aparicio ORIS Success Code — encompassing the four dimensions of **Offense** (proximity to orbital/cranial structures), **Rehabilitation** (functional and prosthetic outcome), **Infection** (sinus or soft-tissue complications), and **Stability** (implant mobility or bone loss) — should be formally scored at Day 30 and at each subsequent recall; a score of 0 across all dimensions indicates an uncomplicated, successful outcome, while any score of 2 or above in the Infection or Stability dimension triggers immediate clinical intervention. Suture type, tension-free closure technique, and post-operative pharmacological protocol (analgesics, antibiotics, corticosteroids) are pending surgical data submission.

---

> **Implant In-Charge Action Required:** Phase 1 has not yet received final sign-off. The above surgical planning sections (G through K) cannot be formally executed until Phase 1 approval is granted by both the supervising clinician and the implant in-charge. Proceeding to surgery without this gate being closed represents a protocol deviation and will not be captured in the audit log as approved. Please review outstanding Phase 1 data, confirm ZAGA classification per side, medical clearance, and implant system selection, then issue your approval to advance this case.
